summary: Mistral released OCR 4, a new version of its document-parsing OCR model adding bounding boxes, block classification and confidence scores, priced via API and Document AI, with published benchmark and human-evaluation results.

practices.reason: The new OCR model is stated to beat competing OCR/document-AI systems on human preference and benchmark scores while being cheaper and faster, making it a candidate to swap into document-ingestion pipelines.
practices.quote: Independent annotators prefer OCR 4 over every leading OCR and document-AI system tested, with win rates averaging 72%, alongside the top overall score on OlmOCRBench (85.20).

practices.reason: The post details a human-preference evaluation methodology and discloses specific, transferable failure modes in automated OCR benchmarks that a team could use to design its own evaluation.
practices.quote: We assembled 600+ documents across 12+ languages, sourced from third-party vendors to represent real industry use cases, and asked independent annotators to blindly rank each competitor's output against OCR 4's, document by document.

practices.reason: New model version, API pricing tiers, and multi-platform availability (SageMaker, Microsoft Foundry) mean teams integrating OCR would need to review endpoints, schema options and deployment mode.
practices.quote: Both Mistral OCRv4 and Document AI (powered by OCRv4) are available via API through Mistral Studio , Amazon SageMaker, Microsoft Foundry , and coming soon Snowflake Parse Document.
